Summary:
Discussion with the Site Management Committee – Water Network Extension Initiative, Al-Fajr Site

During the discussion, the Site Management Committee (SMC) members raised the issue of water access as one of the most pressing challenges facing residents of Al-Fajr Site. They explained that several sections of the site remain unconnected to the existing water distribution network, forcing many households to walk long distances to reach the nearest water collection point. Committee members emphasized that this places an additional burden on displaced families, particularly vulnerable groups such as older persons, persons with disabilities, women, and children. They also noted that the limited quantity of available water prevents many households from meeting their daily water needs on a consistent basis.
In response to these concerns, the proposed initiative was discussed with the committee as a means of addressing these urgent needs by extending the water distribution network to the currently underserved sections of the site. The SMC members agreed that this intervention would ensure a more equitable distribution of water, reduce the time and effort required for water collection, and provide households with easier and more reliable access to this essential service.
The discussion also covered the procurement of an electrical cable to connect an additional water well located at a distance from the existing well. Committee members confirmed that the municipality provides a generator with sufficient capacity to operate both wells simultaneously, and that connecting the second well would allow both wells to operate at the same time, increasing water production capacity and improving the continuity and reliability of the water supply throughout the site.
At the conclusion of the discussion, the SMC members expressed their strong support for the initiative, noting that it is expected to enhance the efficiency of the site's water distribution system, increase the amount of water available to residents, ensure that all sections of the site are adequately served, and reduce the burden on displaced households in accessing water. The committee agreed that the initiative will contribute to improving the overall living conditions and public health of more than 1,250 displaced households residing at Al-Fajr Site.

Topic: Programming Specific Meetings (e.g. project inductions, cash for work, etc.)
Summary: A coordination meeting was conducted by ACTED's Site Management team at Al Jawhari Site with representatives from Al Fedaa, Al Bwasil, and Al Shaheed Jameel displacement sites to prepare for the implementation of Community-Led Initiatives (CLIs). The session focused on strengthening the administrative and financial readiness of site representatives by introducing the implementation procedures, clarifying documentation requirements, and reinforcing accountability throughout the initiative lifecycle. Participants received comprehensive guidance on the financial management process, including procurement procedures, the mandatory use of official tax invoices, supplier documentation, payment verification, and labor payment records to ensure compliance with project requirements and donor standards. To facilitate standardized implementation, ACTED distributed the complete set of financial and administrative templates required for the CLIs, including supplier invoices, delivery receipts, payment acknowledgments, workers' attendance sheets, worker payment forms, and final supplier declarations. The meeting also provided an opportunity to address site-specific implementation questions. Representatives from Al Fedaa Site discussed the planned procurement of furniture under their initiative and confirmed that it would complement, rather than duplicate, the furniture support to be provided separately by ACTED, ensuring efficient use of available resources while enhancing activities for children and community members. Throughout the session, ACTED emphasized the importance of transparent financial management, adherence to approved budgets, timely implementation, and continuous coordination between site representatives and the Site Management team. To strengthen communication and facilitate real-time follow-up during implementation, dedicated WhatsApp groups were established for each initiative, enabling rapid coordination, technical support, and administrative guidance. The meeting concluded with agreement from all participants to begin implementation promptly while complying with the established financial procedures and documentation requirements. التاريخ: 21/07/2026
نوع النشاط: جلسة توعية (Awareness Session)
في ظل الضغوط النفسية والاجتماعية المتزايدة التي تعيشها الأسر النازحة نتيجة ظروف النزوح المستمرة، نُفذت جلسة توعوية استهدفت أرباب الأسر بهدف تعزيز الوعي بالصحة النفسية، وتنمية القدرة على التعامل مع الضغوط والانفعالات بما ينعكس إيجابًا على الاستقرار الأسري والمجتمعي.
أهداف الجلسة
•	تعزيز الوعي بأهمية الصحة النفسية في حياة الفرد والأسرة. 
•	التعريف بمفهوم اضطرابات الشخصية والفرق بينها وبين الاضطرابات النفسية الأخرى. 
•	توضيح أبرز أنواع اضطرابات الشخصية وخصائصها العامة. 
•	تنمية مهارات إدارة الضغوط والانفعالات. 
•	تشجيع المشاركين على طلب المساعدة النفسية المتخصصة عند الحاجة. 
•	تعزيز أساليب التواصل الإيجابي داخل الأسرة. 
آلية تنفيذ النشاط
افتتحت الجلسة بالتعريف بمفهوم الصحة النفسية وأهميتها في مواجهة التحديات اليومية داخل بيئة النزوح، ثم قدم المدرب شرحًا مبسطًا حول اضطرابات الشخصية، مع توضيح الفروق بينها وبين الاضطرابات النفسية الأخرى بطريقة تناسب المشاركين.
كما تناولت الجلسة تأثير الضغوط المستمرة على السلوك والعلاقات الأسرية، واستعرضت مجموعة من الأساليب العملية لإدارة التوتر، والتحكم بالغضب، والتعامل مع الضغوط اليومية، بالإضافة إلى أهمية الحوار الأسري والدعم المتبادل بين أفراد الأسرة.
وتخللت الورشة مناقشات جماعية أتاحت للمشاركين مشاركة تجاربهم اليومية، وطرح أبرز التحديات التي تواجههم في ظل ظروف النزوح، حيث تم تقديم إرشادات عملية تساعدهم على التعامل مع تلك التحديات بصورة أكثر إيجابية.
النتائج المحققة
•	زيادة وعي المشاركين بمفاهيم الصحة النفسية. 
•	تحسين فهمهم لاضطرابات الشخصية وآثارها على العلاقات الاجتماعية. 
•	تعزيز مهارات التحكم بالانفعالات وإدارة الضغوط. 
•	تشجيع المشاركين على تبني أساليب تواصل أكثر إيجابية داخل الأسرة. 
•	رفع مستوى تقبل فكرة اللجوء إلى الدعم النفسي عند الحاجة. 
الخلاصة
حققت الورشة أهدافها في تعزيز الوعي بالصحة النفسية لدى المشاركين، وأسهمت في تزويدهم بمهارات عملية تساعدهم على التعامل مع الضغوط اليومية، بما ينعكس إيجابًا على استقرار الأسرة وتحسين العلاقات الاجتماعية داخل الموقع.
التوصيات
•	الاستمرار في تنفيذ جلسات الدعم النفسي والتوعية المجتمعية. 
•	تنظيم ورش متخصصة حول إدارة الضغوط النفسية والتربية الإيجابية. 
•	تعزيز الإحالة إلى خدمات الدعم النفسي للحالات التي تحتاج إلى متابعة. 
•	تشجيع الأنشطة المجتمعية التي تعزز التماسك الاجتماعي والدعم المتبادل بين الأسر. 
•	إدماج موضوعات الصحة النفسية ضمن الأنشطة التوعوية الدورية داخل الموقع.

Summary: A coordination meeting was held with representatives of the Al Bwasil Site Community-Led Initiative (CLI) to review the proposed water supply solution before implementation. During the discussion, an initial proposal was presented to connect the new water network to two separate sources: the Emirati water pipeline and a nearby groundwater well. The objective was to use the well as the primary water source while maintaining the Emirati pipeline as a secondary backup, allowing site residents to benefit from both sources whenever available. However, following further technical discussions and verification during the meeting, it was confirmed that the Emirati water pipeline does not provide a reliable and continuous water supply. Based on this assessment, participants collectively agreed to adopt the more sustainable option by relying on the on-site well as the primary water source for the initiative. This decision ensures a more reliable water supply, enhances the long-term sustainability of the intervention, and maximizes the benefit for the displaced community while reducing the risk of service interruptions.

في إطار أنشطة مشروع الإدارة الشاملة للمواقع والحماية للمجتمعات النازحة في قطاع غزة، وضمن التدخلات الهادفة إلى تحسين مستوى السلامة والحماية داخل مواقع النزوح، تم تنفيذ نشاط توزيع عدد 218 كشافًا على الأسر المقيمة في موقع إيواء الجليس.
ثانيًا: الإجراءات التي سبقت عملية التوزيع
سبق تنفيذ عملية التوزيع مجموعة من الإجراءات والأنشطة الميدانية التي نفذها فريق المشروع، بهدف ضمان دقة الاستهداف ووصول الكشافات إلى المستفيدين بصورة منظمة وعادلة.
وشملت هذه الإجراءات:
تنفيذ مسح ميداني داخل الموقع للتعرف إلى أوضاع الأسر واحتياجاتها المتعلقة بالإنارة. 
حصر الأسر المقيمة وتحديث بياناتها بالتنسيق مع لجنة إدارة الموقع وممثلي السكان. 
مراجعة قوائم المستفيدين والتحقق من صحة البيانات المسجلة. 
التأكد من عدم وجود تكرار في الأسماء أو البيانات. 
ترتيب المستفيدين وفق القوائم المعتمدة وآلية التوزيع المحددة. 
التنسيق المسبق مع لجنة إدارة الموقع بشأن موعد التوزيع ومكانه وآلية تنظيم حضور المستفيدين. 
توعية اللجنة والمستفيدين بضرورة الالتزام بالنظام والتعليمات أثناء عملية التسليم.
ثالثاَ : تنفيذ عملية التوزيع
بعد الانتهاء من أعمال المسح الميداني والتحقق من بيانات المستفيدين واعتماد القوائم النهائية، تم التنسيق مع لجنة إدارة الموقع لإبلاغ الأسر المستهدفة بموعد ومكان استلام الكشافات.
وقد نُفذت عملية التوزيع في نقطة توزيع معتمدة تابعة لمركز معا التنموي، حيث حضر المستفيدون وفق المواعيد المحددة، وتمت مطابقة بياناتهم مع القوائم المعتمدة قبل تسليمهم الكشافات، مع استكمال إجراءات التوثيق والتوقيع على كشوفات الاستلام وفق الإجراءات المعتمدة.
وقد جرت عملية التوزيع بصورة منظمة، وبالتنسيق بين فريق المشروع ولجنة إدارة الموقع، بما ضمن سهولة الإجراءات ووصول الكشافات إلى المستفيدين المستهدفين بكل شفافية وعدالة.
رابعًا: دور لجنة إدارة الموقع
ساهمت لجنة إدارة الموقع في دعم عملية التنفيذ من خلال:
التنسيق مع الأسر وإبلاغها بموعد ومكان التوزيع. 
المساهمة في مراجعة البيانات والتحقق من المستفيدين. 
تنظيم حضور الأسر ودعم فريق المشروع خلال عملية التسليم. 
توضيح آلية التوزيع للسكان والرد على الاستفسارات الأولية. 
نقل الملاحظات أو الحالات التي احتاجت إلى مراجعة إلى فريق المشروع. 
وقد ساهم هذا التعاون في تنفيذ النشاط بصورة منظمة وتقليل الازدحام وتعزيز الشفافية والمشاركة المجتمعية.
خامسًا: أهمية النشاط
ساهم نشاط توزيع الكشافات في تلبية جزء من احتياجات الأسر المتعلقة بالإنارة، وخاصة في ظل ضعف أو انقطاع مصادر الكهرباء داخل الموقع.
ومن المتوقع أن يسهم النشاط في:
تحسين قدرة الأسر على الإنارة داخل الخيام والمساكن المؤقتة. 
تعزيز السلامة أثناء الحركة داخل الموقع خلال ساعات الليل. 
الحد من مخاطر التعثر أو السقوط في الممرات والمناطق غير المضاءة. 
دعم احتياجات النساء والأطفال وكبار السن والأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة. .
تحسين الظروف المعيشية اليومية للأسر المستفيدة. 
سادسًا: الملاحظات
تمت عملية التوزيع بصورة منظمة وفق القوائم المعتمدة، مع الالتزام بإجراءات التحقق والتوثيق. كما أبدى المستفيدون تعاونًا خلال عملية التسليم، وأكدت لجنة إدارة الموقع أهمية استمرار التدخلات التي تعالج احتياجات الإنارة والسلامة داخل الموقع.
سابعًا: المخرجات
استكمال المسح الميداني والتحقق من بيانات المستفيدين. 
اعتماد القوائم النهائية للأسر المستهدفة. 
توزيع عدد 218 كشافًا على المستفيدين. 
توثيق عملية الاستلام وفق الإجراءات المعتمدة. 
تعزيز التعاون بين فريق المشروع ولجنة إدارة الموقع. 
المساهمة في تحسين مستوى الإنارة والسلامة داخل الموقع. 
ثامنًا: التوصيات
الاستمرار في تحديث بيانات الأسر داخل الموقع. 
مواصلة رصد احتياجات الإنارة والطاقة داخل المخيم. 
تعزيز دور لجنة إدارة الموقع في متابعة احتياجات السكان والتنسيق مع الجهات المختصة. 
دراسة إمكانية تنفيذ تدخلات إضافية للإنارة في الممرات والمساحات المشتركة داخل الموقع.

A rodent and insect control and environmental health improvement intervention was implemented at Al-Mahabba Displacement Site, targeting 153 tents accommodating displaced families. The activities included spraying the interior and exterior surroundings of the tents, pathways, and communal areas using an insecticide containing 20% Cypermethrin, diluted with water at a ratio of 20 ml per litre. The site’s external perimeter was also treated with STOPER rodent-repellent granules.

In addition, Pastion Plus rodent-control bait, containing the active ingredient Brodifacoum, was distributed at a rate of two 12-gram pieces per tent. The bait was placed in safe and concealed locations, away from children, food items, and water sources.

Prior to the commencement of the control activities, families received a refresher briefing reinforcing the awareness and safety messages delivered during the first round of the intervention, rather than participating in new awareness sessions. The briefing covered the necessary preparations before spraying the tents and the site, safe practices during implementation, ventilation and cleaning procedures, and the conditions for safely re-entering tents after spraying. Families were also reminded of the risks associated with touching insecticides or rodent bait and were instructed to immediately report any exposure incident or concern to the site team.

The intervention was implemented in accordance with the principles of protection, do no harm, and human dignity, with particular attention given to the safety of children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other individuals at heightened risk. Families were instructed to keep children, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and individuals with specific health conditions away from spraying areas. They were also advised not to place insecticides or rodent bait near sleeping areas, food preparation spaces, or water-storage facilities.

The activity further emphasized the rights of women and children to access a safe and healthy environment. Safety information was communicated in a clear and appropriate manner, while ensuring privacy, non-discrimination, and opportunities for families to raise questions and submit feedback or complaints related to the intervention.

The intervention was implemented in coordination with the site management and other relevant stakeholders. It contributed to reducing the prevalence of rodents and insects and mitigating the associated health and environmental risks, thereby enhancing the safety of displaced families and improving health and living conditions within the displacement site.

The intervention was implemented by Acted through the Cash-for-Work programme, engaging members of the displaced community residing within the site to undertake priority maintenance and improvement activities. Workers were provided with the required maintenance tools, cleaning equipment, construction materials, and personal protective equipment supplied by Acted to support the implementation of planned activities and improve site conditions.  

Following the distribution of Site Maintenance, Improvements and Cleaning Tools, workers carried out a range of maintenance and rehabilitation activities throughout the site. The equipment package included ladders, wooden pallets, steel net rolls, shovels, hoes, rakes, wheelbarrows, brooms, tarpaulins, steel sheets, ropes, sandbags, hand tools, cleaning materials, personal protective equipment, fire safety equipment, and first aid supplies. These materials supported pathway maintenance, shelter repairs, drainage improvements, sanitation works, cleaning campaigns, and site rehabilitation activities.  

Throughout the intervention period, activities were directly supervised by site supervisors responsible for organizing workers and allocating tasks according to operational priorities. Acted’s engineering team regularly monitored implementation to ensure compliance with technical standards, safety procedures, and the approved work plan. In addition, the Site Maintenance Committee actively supported the identification of priority needs and coordinated interventions aimed at improving safety, accessibility, and living conditions for displaced households.  

The intervention resulted in significant improvements across the site. A total of 55 pathways were cleaned and 50 pathways were leveled and improved to facilitate safer movement within the site. Workers installed 695 sandbags and constructed 256 protective sandbag barriers to reduce risks associated with weather conditions and protect shelters. In addition, 20 pits were backfilled, 4 absorption pits were maintained, and 5 sanitation manholes were repaired. Shelter maintenance activities included the repair of 25 tents and the erection of 4 additional tents. The team also maintained 5 community service points and removed approximately 130 cubic meters of rubble and waste from the site, contributing to a safer and cleaner living environment for residents. These activities directly benefited 67 displaced families living in the site. 

The works were implemented by 18 Cash-for-Work participants, including 5 women and 13 men, over a total of 270 labour days. The intervention provided temporary income opportunities while simultaneously supporting the improvement of essential infrastructure and services within the site.  

Prior to the commencement of field activities, participants attended awareness sessions covering occupational health and safety measures, security procedures, work organization, and implementation modalities. In addition, ACTED’s MEAL team delivered awareness sessions on the Accountability and Feedback Mechanism (AFM), ensuring that participants were informed about available feedback channels and accountability procedures throughout the implementation period.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Summary:
في ظل الظروف البيئية والصحية التي يعيشها النازحون داخل الموقع، وما يرافقها من تزايد انتشار القوارض والأمراض الجلدية الناتجة عن الاكتظاظ وضعف خدمات الصرف الصحي وتراكم النفايات، تم تنفيذ جلسة توعوية استهدفت السيدات باعتبارهن الأكثر ارتباطًا بإدارة شؤون الأسرة والعناية بالأطفال، بهدف رفع مستوى الوعي الصحي وتعزيز السلوكيات الوقائية داخل الأسر.
أهداف الجلسة
•	رفع مستوى الوعي بالمخاطر الصحية الناتجة عن انتشار القوارض داخل مواقع النزوح.
•	تعريف المشاركات بأنواع القوارض الأكثر انتشارًا والأضرار التي تسببها.
•	توضيح الأمراض الجلدية الشائعة في بيئة النزوح وأسباب انتشارها.
•	تعزيز ممارسات النظافة الشخصية ونظافة البيئة المحيطة.
•	تشجيع الأسر على الإبلاغ المبكر عن المخاطر الصحية والبيئية داخل الموقع.
آلية تنفيذ النشاط
•	بدأت الجلسة بالتعريف بموضوع الورشة وأهدافها، ثم ناقش فريق التوعية مع المشاركات أبرز المشكلات الصحية التي تواجه الأسر داخل الموقع، مع إتاحة الفرصة للمشاركات لعرض تجاربهن اليومية.
•	بعد ذلك تم استعراض أنواع القوارض المنتشرة، وشرح الأمراض التي قد تنقلها، إضافة إلى توضيح الإجراءات الوقائية مثل حفظ الطعام بطريقة آمنة، والتخلص السليم من النفايات، وسد الفتحات التي قد تتخذها القوارض مأوى لها.
•	كما تناولت الجلسة الأمراض الجلدية الأكثر انتشارًا بين الأطفال والبالغين، مع شرح أسباب الإصابة بها، وطرق الوقاية والعناية بالنظافة الشخصية، وأهمية مراجعة المراكز الصحية عند ظهور أعراض تستدعي التدخل الطبي.
•	واختُتمت الجلسة بحوار مفتوح للإجابة عن استفسارات المشاركات وتقديم الإرشادات المناسبة للحالات التي تم طرحها.
النتائج المحققة
•	زيادة وعي المشاركات بالمخاطر الصحية المرتبطة بالقوارض.
•	تعزيز المعرفة بالممارسات الوقائية التي تحد من انتشار الأمراض.
•	رفع مستوى الوعي بأهمية النظافة الشخصية والبيئية.
•	تشجيع السيدات على نقل الرسائل التوعوية إلى أفراد أسرهن وجيرانهن.
•	تعزيز التواصل بين المجتمع والجهات الإنسانية فيما يتعلق بالإبلاغ عن المشكلات البيئية.
الخلاصة
ساهمت الورشة في تحسين مستوى الوعي الصحي لدى المشاركات، وزيادة إدراكهن لأهمية الإجراءات الوقائية داخل الأسرة، الأمر الذي يسهم في الحد من انتشار الأمراض وتعزيز بيئة صحية وآمنة داخل الموقع.
التوصيات
•	تنفيذ جلسات متابعة دورية حول الصحة العامة والوقاية من الأمراض.
•	دعم حملات مكافحة القوارض داخل الموقع.
•	تعزيز حملات النظافة وإدارة النفايات.

نُفذت ورشة توعوية حول الأمراض الجلدية استهدفت السيدات، بهدف تعزيز الوعي بأكثر الأمراض الجلدية انتشارًا، وبيان أسبابها وطرق انتقالها، إضافة إلى نشر الممارسات الصحية التي تساهم في الوقاية منها والحفاظ على صحة أفراد الأسرة.

النتائج
رفع مستوى الوعي لدى المشاركات حول الأمراض الجلدية الشائعة.
تعزيز المعرفة بأسباب الإصابة وطرق الوقاية.
تشجيع السيدات على تبني ممارسات صحية تقلل من خطر انتقال العدوى.
زيادة الوعي بأهمية التشخيص المبكر وطلب الرعاية الصحية عند الحاجة.

عدد المشاركين: 35 طفلًا
نوع النشاط: جلسة توعية (Awareness Session)
نفذت جمعية المستقبل الشبابي ورشة توعوية للأطفال بهدف تعزيز الوعي بمخاطر المواد المتفجرة ومخلفات الحروب، وتنمية السلوكيات الآمنة التي تساعد الأطفال على حماية أنفسهم وتجنب التعرض للحوادث، وذلك من خلال تقديم معلومات مبسطة تتناسب مع أعمارهم.
مجريات الورشة
بدأت الورشة بالتعريف بالمواد المتفجرة ومخلفات الحروب، مع توضيح أن هذه الأجسام قد تكون موجودة في أماكن مختلفة وتشكل خطرًا كبيرًا حتى وإن بدت قديمة أو غير فعالة. وتم التأكيد على أهمية عدم الاقتراب من أي جسم مجهول أو لمسه أو تحريكه تحت أي ظرف.
كما تضمنت الورشة شرح الخطوات الصحيحة التي ينبغي اتباعها عند مشاهدة جسم يشتبه بأنه خطر، وتشمل الابتعاد عن المكان، وتحذير الآخرين من الاقتراب، وإبلاغ شخص بالغ أو الجهات المختصة دون محاولة التعامل مع الجسم. وتم استخدام وسائل توضيحية ونقاشات تفاعلية وأمثلة تناسب الفئة العمرية المستهدفة لتعزيز فهم الأطفال للرسائل الأساسية.
النتائج
زيادة وعي الأطفال بمخاطر المواد المتفجرة ومخلفات الحروب.
تعريف المشاركين بالسلوكيات الآمنة عند العثور على أجسام مشبوهة.
تعزيز ثقافة الإبلاغ وعدم العبث بالأجسام المجهولة.
تنمية إحساس الأطفال بالمسؤولية تجاه حماية أنفسهم والآخرين.
تحقيق تفاعل إيجابي من الأطفال من خلال المشاركة في الأنشطة والنقاشات.
التوصيات
الاستمرار في تنفيذ برامج التوعية الخاصة بالسلامة للأطفال بشكل دوري.
إشراك أولياء الأمور في الأنشطة التوعوية لتعزيز الرسائل الوقائية داخل الأسرة.
توزيع مواد توعوية مبسطة تساعد الأطفال على تذكر قواعد السلامة.
تعزيز التعاون مع المدارس والمراكز المجتمعية لنشر الوعي بمخاطر مخلفات الحروب.
الخلاصة
حققت الورشة أهدافها في رفع مستوى وعي الأطفال بمخاطر المواد المتفجرة، وتعزيز السلوكيات الوقائية التي تساعدهم على تجنب الحوادث، مما يسهم في توفير بيئة أكثر أمانًا للأطفال والمجتمع.

مقدمة
ضمن سلسلة الاجتماعات المجتمعية السابقة المنفذة مع سكان مخيم سلام الشمال، وبالتنسيق مع أعضاء المجتمع المحلي وممثلي السكان، تم مناقشة أبرز الاحتياجات والتحديات التي تواجه الأسر داخل الموقع، حيث تم التأكيد على وجود احتياج ملح لدى عدد من كبار السن والأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة الذين يواجهون صعوبة في الحركة والنوم على الأرض أو استخدام الوسائل المتوفرة حاليًا، مما يؤثر على راحتهم اليومية ويزيد من صعوبة تلبية احتياجاتهم الأساسية.
وخلال النقاشات المجتمعية، تم تحديد ضرورة توفير أسرّة مناسبة لهذه الفئة باعتبارها من الفئات الأكثر ضعفًا، وذلك بهدف تحسين ظروف معيشتهم، وتسهيل الحركة والتنقل، وتقليل المعاناة اليومية، بالإضافة إلى الحفاظ على كرامتهم الإنسانية وتوفير بيئة معيشية أكثر ملاءمة لهم داخل الموقع.
وبناءً على هذا الاحتياج الذي تم تحديده من خلال المجتمع، تم رفع طلب لتوفير مشاطيح خشبية ضمن تدخلات قسم المأوى (Shelter)، لاستخدامها في تصنيع أسرّة مخصصة لكبار السن والأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة الذين لديهم حاجة ماسة لهذا التدخل.
تحديد الاحتياج

الملاحظات الميدانية خلال الزيارات والاجتماعات المجتمعية مع سكان الموقع.
النقاشات مع الأسر حول أبرز التحديات التي تواجه الفئات الأكثر ضعفًا.
وجود عدد من كبار السن والأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة غير القادرين على استخدام أماكن النوم التقليدية داخل الخيام.
الحاجة إلى توفير حلول بسيطة وعملية تساعد على تحسين مستوى الراحة والحركة داخل أماكن الإقامة.

كبار السن الذين يعانون من صعوبة في الحركة.
الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة الذين يحتاجون إلى تسهيل التنقل والنوم.
الحالات التي لا تتوفر لديها وسائل نوم مناسبة.

تسهيل الحركة وتقليل الصعوبات اليومية التي تواجه هذه الفئات.
تعزيز الحماية والكرامة الإنسانية للأسر المستفيدة.
دعم جهود إدارة الموقع في الاستجابة للاحتياجات ذات الأولوية التي يحددها المجتمع.

توفير المشاطيح المطلوبة وتجهيز الأسرّة داخل الموقع.
متابعة استخدام الأسرّة والتأكد من وصولها للفئات المستهدفة.
توثيق المستفيدين ضمن سجلات إدارة الموقع.

تحسين مستوى الراحة والخصوصية للمستفيدين.
تقليل الصعوبات المرتبطة بالنوم والحركة داخل الخيام.
تعزيز مشاركة المجتمع في تحديد وتنفيذ التدخلات ذات الأولوية.

التاريخ: 15/07/2026
الجهة المنفذة: UNICEF
الفئة المستهدفة: السيدات
عدد المشاركات: 20 سيدة
مقدمة
في إطار تعزيز الوعي الصحي داخل مواقع النزوح، تم تنفيذ ورشة توعوية حول مخاطر القوارض وطرق الوقاية منها، استهدفت السيدات في موقع العزة باعتبارهن عنصرًا أساسيًا في تطبيق الممارسات الصحية داخل الأسر.
أهداف الورشة
التعريف بمخاطر القوارض وتأثيرها الصحي.
توعية المشاركات بطرق الوقاية.
تعزيز الممارسات الصحية داخل الخيام.
الحد من انتشار الأمراض المرتبطة بالقوارض.
مجريات الورشة
تناولت الورشة أسباب انتشار القوارض داخل مواقع النزوح، والمخاطر الصحية الناتجة عنها، إضافة إلى مناقشة طرق الوقاية، ومنها:
حفظ الأغذية بطريقة آمنة.
التخلص السليم من النفايات.
تنظيف محيط الخيام.
إغلاق الفتحات التي قد تسمح بدخول القوارض.
الإبلاغ عن أماكن انتشار القوارض.
كما شاركت السيدات في النقاش وطرح التجارب والمشكلات التي تواجههن داخل الموقع.
المخرجات
رفع مستوى الوعي الصحي لدى المشاركات.
تعزيز السلوكيات الوقائية.
نقل الرسائل الصحية إلى أفراد الأسرة.
التوصيات
استمرار تنفيذ جلسات التوعية الصحية.
تنفيذ حملات لمكافحة القوارض.
تحسين إدارة النفايات داخل الموقع.

الهدف من التدخل:
إشارة إلى اجتماع اللجنة الذي تم تنفيذه داخل موقع العزة بمشاركة عدد من أعضاء لجنة الموقع والمجتمع المحلي بتاريخ 29/6/2026 برزت الاحتياج الضروري لإنشاء أثاث يتكون من كراسي ومكاتب وخزانة لخيمة الإدارة وذلك من خلال استخدام المشاطيح.

مبررات الاحتياج:
لوحظ الحاجة إلى توفير بيئة مناسبة تُمكّن فريق إدارة الموقع من أداء مهامه اليومية بكفاءة. ويُعد توفير مكاتب  داخل الموقع أمرًا ضروريًا لدعم العمل الميداني وضمان استمرارية إدارة الموقع بشكل منظم وفعّال، خاصة في ظل الضغط التشغيلي وارتفاع وتيرة الاحتياجات الإنسانية. يسهم وجود مكتب مُجهّز في تسهيل استقبال النازحين/ات والاستماع إلى شكاواهم وملاحظاتهم بطريقة تحفظ الكرامة والخصوصية، كما يتيح تنظيم عمليات التنسيق والإحالة مع الشركاء الإنسانيين والقطاعات المختلفة، بما ينسجم مع نهج مشروع الإدارة الشاملة للمواقع والحماية للمجتمعات النازحة في قطاع غزة في إدارة المواقع وتعزيز المساءلة أمام المجتمعات المتأثرة.
كما يدعم هذا التجهيز توثيق البيانات والمتابعة اليومية لاحتياجات السكان داخل الموقع، ويُوفر مساحة مناسبة لاجتماعات اللجنة المجتمعية، الأمر الذي يعزز المشاركة المجتمعية،. وعليه، فإن توفير هذه التجهيزات يُعد متطلبًا أساسيًا يسهم في تحسين جودة إدارة الموقع وضمان تقديم خدمات إنسانية أكثر فعالية وشمولية داخل الموقع.

آلية الحل:
تجهيز وتنفيذ صناعة مكاتب وطاولات و رفوف سيتم استخدامهم كأثاث في خيمة إدارة المخيم.

الاحتياجات:
- عدد 20 مشطاح خشبي
التوصيات:
- تجهيز مكتب وكراسي ورفوف لاستخدامها كأثاث داخل خيمة إدارة الموقع والقدرة على تنفيذ النشاطات.

Topic: Community to Site Management Committee Interface Meetings
Summary:
NRC's Site Management (SM) and Shelter teams met with the Site Management Committee (SMC) at Al-Nour Al-Nakheel Site in Khan Younis to discuss the ongoing shelter repair project and community priorities. The committee opened the meeting by expressing appreciation for NRC's interventions at the site and reaffirming a shared commitment to close coordination in support of IDPs and the most vulnerable.
 First, the committee raised concerns regarding households didn’t benefit from the first repair project. The Shelter team clarified that the committee had been invited to nominate any additional eligible households after the field visit, and that the team had also scanned the entire site to ensure no household meeting the criteria was missed.
Second, the committee noted that the selection criteria and scope of the repairs need for more clarifications , particularly concerning deteriorated shelter surroundings that raise privacy concerns. The Shelter team explained that the project targets the repair of the main living area inside the shelter, which is the family's priority, while the reuse of existing materials to improve kitchens, toilets, and surroundings is an added value of the project. Repairing the surroundings requires only tarpaulins and falls outside the project's scope.
Third, regarding the size of the assistance package, the committee suggested it could be divided to reach a greater number of IDPs. The Shelter team clarified that the package was designed for makeshift shelters with poor framing and combines cash assistance (to purchase framing materials at high local market prices) with NFIs (tarpaulins) to produce a dignified and complete shelter. Integrated service reviewed by shelter specialists and aligned with Shelter Cluster recommendations, the package cannot be divided.
Finally, the committee highlighted additional NFI needs — including tarpaulins, tents, kitchen sets, clothing, solar lights, and household-level toilets — and stressed the importance of winterization readiness. The Shelter team acknowledged these needs but explained that the limited resources is the main concern. 
The meeting concluded with mutual understanding of the project's scope and constraints, and continued commitment to coordination between NRC and the committee.

Summary:
A field visit was conducted to the "Namaa" site in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, during which a coordination meeting was held with the site management. Key outcomes of the visit included:

Formation of Representative Committee: Discussed the formation of a local community committee representing the displaced population. Special focus was placed on ensuring inclusive participation, explicitly stipulating a minimum of 30% women representation in the committee membership.

Roles and Responsibilities: Outlined the scope of work, key tasks, and specific responsibilities for the committee members to ensure transparent communication, needs identification, and effective field coordination.

Project Orientation & Capacity Building: Introduced the overarching project objectives and upcoming key activities, emphasizing that the project includes dedicated capacity-building initiatives aimed at strengthening the committee's skills and empowering them to perform their mandate effectively.

A rodent and insect control and environmental health improvement intervention was implemented at Metro Al-Jawazat Site Displacement Site, targeting 770 tents accommodating displaced families. The activities included spraying the interior and exterior surroundings of the tents, pathways, and communal areas using an insecticide containing 20% Cypermethrin, diluted with water at a ratio of 20 ml per litre. The site’s external perimeter was also treated with STOPER rodent-repellent granules.

In addition, Pastion Plus rodent-control bait, containing the active ingredient Brodifacoum, was distributed at a rate of two 12-gram pieces per tent. The bait was placed in safe and concealed locations, away from children, food items, and water sources.

Prior to the commencement of the control activities, families received a refresher briefing reinforcing the awareness and safety messages delivered during the first round of the intervention, rather than participating in new awareness sessions. The briefing covered the necessary preparations before spraying the tents and the site, safe practices during implementation, ventilation and cleaning procedures, and the conditions for safely re-entering tents after spraying. Families were also reminded of the risks associated with touching insecticides or rodent bait and were instructed to immediately report any exposure incident or concern to the site team.

The intervention was implemented in accordance with the principles of protection, do no harm, and human dignity, with particular attention given to the safety of children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other individuals at heightened risk. Families were instructed to keep children, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and individuals with specific health conditions away from spraying areas. They were also advised not to place insecticides or rodent bait near sleeping areas, food preparation spaces, or water-storage facilities.

The activity further emphasized the rights of women and children to access a safe and healthy environment. Safety information was communicated in a clear and appropriate manner, while ensuring privacy, non-discrimination, and opportunities for families to raise questions and submit feedback or complaints related to the intervention.

The intervention was implemented in coordination with the site management and other relevant stakeholders. It contributed to reducing the prevalence of rodents and insects and mitigating the associated health and environmental risks, thereby enhancing the safety of displaced families and improving health and living conditions within the displacement site.

تم يوم الأحد الموافق 9/8/2026 تنفيذ اليوم الأول من تدريب لجنة إدارة الموقع (SMC) في موقع نازحي الشمال، بمشاركة 13 متدربًا (10 رجال و3 سيدات).

تناول التدريب مفهوم إدارة مواقع النزوح (CCCM)، وتعريف مواقع النزوح وآليات إدارتها، وتنظيم وتنسيق المساعدات الإنسانية، بما يشمل مبادئ العدالة والإنصاف في توزيع المساعدات، وتحديد الأولويات وفق الاحتياجات، وضمان وصول المساعدات للفئات الأكثر ضعفًا، إضافة إلى التعريف بآلية MapServ ودورها في دعم إدارة المواقع والاستجابة للاحتياجات.

كما تم تنفيذ التقييم القبلي، إلى جانب أنشطة تفاعلية وعصف ذهني ونقاشات مع المتدربين حول واقع إدارة الموقع والتحديات القائمة وسبل تحسين الاستجابة.

وقد لاقى التدريب استحسانًا عامًا وتفاعلًا إيجابيًا من المشاركين، بما يعزز دور لجنة إدارة الموقع في تحسين التنسيق والاستجابة داخل الموقع.

تم يوم الاثنين الموافق 10/8/2026 تنفيذ اليوم الثاني والأخير من تدريب لجنة إدارة الموقع (SMC) في موقع نازحي الشمال، بمشاركة 13 متدربًا (10 رجال و3 سيدات).

تناول التدريب موضوع المساءلة أمام المجتمعات المتضررة (AAP) وتعزيز الشفافية والمشاركة المجتمعية، إضافة إلى آليات الشكاوى والتغذية الراجعة (CFM) وكيفية استقبال الشكاوى والتعامل معها بسرية وحيادية، بما يضمن الاستجابة المناسبة ومتابعة الملاحظات والشكاوى. كما تم التطرق إلى مبادئ الحماية وآليات الإحالة، والتعرف على كيفية تحديد حالات الحماية وربطها بالجهات المختصة وفق الإجراءات المعتمدة.

تم تنفيذ التقييم البعدي، إلى جانب مجموعة من الأنشطة التفاعلية والعصف الذهني والنقاشات حول واقع إدارة الموقع والتحديات القائمة، وسبل تعزيز الحماية والإحالات والمساءلة داخل الموقع.

وفي ختام التدريب، تم عقد نقاش مفتوح مع المشاركين، حيث عبّروا عن تقديرهم واستحسانهم للتدريب، وأكدوا أهمية استمرار مثل هذه التدريبات في بناء قدرات أعضاء لجنة إدارة الموقع وتعزيز قدرتهم على أداء أدوارهم بكفاءة وفاعلية.

On Thursday, August 13, 2026, the first day of the training program for the "Site Management Committee" (SMC) was held at the "Taiba Educational Site," with the participation of 12 trainees (8 men and 4 women).
The training focused on the concept of "Camp Coordination and Camp Management" (CCCM) and the mechanisms for managing and coordinating humanitarian aid based on principles of justice, equity, and prioritization. Participants were also introduced to the "MapServ" mechanism and its role in supporting site management and addressing specific needs.
The training included a pre-assessment, interactive activities, and discussions regarding the site's current situation, key challenges, and ways to enhance the response. The participants engaged positively, contributing to the strengthening of the committee's capabilities and its role in effectively managing the site.

On Sunday, August 16, 2026, the second and final day of the training program for the Site Management Committee (SMC) was held at the " Nasa'im Al Khair" site, with the participation of 12 trainees (8 men and 4 women).

The training focused on reinforcing concepts of Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), transparency, and community engagement, as well as Complaint and Feedback Mechanisms (CFM), protection principles, referral mechanisms, and the safe, confidential handling of protection cases.

The training also included interactive activities and discussions regarding the challenges facing site management and ways to enhance response, accountability, and protection. The program concluded with a post-training assessment and an open discussion session, during which participants expressed their appreciation for the training and emphasized its importance in strengthening the committee's capabilities and enabling its members to perform their roles effectively and efficiently.

This intervention supports the site management committee’s efforts to maintain site preparedness and enhance the safety of displaced families.

This intervention supports the site management committee’s efforts to maintain site preparedness and enhance the safety of displaced families.

A rodent and insect control and environmental health improvement intervention (Round 2)  was implemented at Ard Abu Salim Displacement Site, targeting 118 tents accommodating displaced families. The activities included spraying the interior and exterior surroundings of the tents, pathways, and communal areas using an insecticide containing 20% Cypermethrin, diluted with water at a ratio of 20 ml per litre. The site’s external perimeter was also treated with STOPER rodent-repellent granules.

In addition, Pastion Plus rodent-control bait, containing the active ingredient Brodifacoum, was distributed at a rate of two 12-gram pieces per tent. The bait was placed in safe and concealed locations, away from children, food items, and water sources.

Prior to the commencement of the control activities, families received a refresher briefing reinforcing the awareness and safety messages delivered during the first round of the intervention, rather than participating in new awareness sessions. The briefing covered the necessary preparations before spraying the tents and the site, safe practices during implementation, ventilation and cleaning procedures, and the conditions for safely re-entering tents after spraying. Families were also reminded of the risks associated with touching insecticides or rodent bait and were instructed to immediately report any exposure incident or concern to the site team.

The intervention was implemented in accordance with the principles of protection, do no harm, and human dignity, with particular attention given to the safety of children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other individuals at heightened risk. Families were instructed to keep children, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and individuals with specific health conditions away from spraying areas. They were also advised not to place insecticides or rodent bait near sleeping areas, food preparation spaces, or water-storage facilities.

The activity further emphasized the rights of women and children to access a safe and healthy environment. Safety information was communicated in a clear and appropriate manner, while ensuring privacy, non-discrimination, and opportunities for families to raise questions and submit feedback or complaints related to the intervention.

The intervention was implemented in coordination with the site management and other relevant stakeholders. It contributed to reducing the prevalence of rodents and insects and mitigating the associated health and environmental risks, thereby enhancing the safety of displaced families and improving health and living conditions within the displacement site.

A rodent and insect control and environmental health improvement intervention (Round 2) was implemented at Issa Murad Displacement Site, targeting 93 tents accommodating displaced families. The activities included spraying the interior and exterior surroundings of the tents, pathways, and communal areas using an insecticide containing 20% Cypermethrin, diluted with water at a ratio of 20 ml per litre. The site’s external perimeter was also treated with STOPER rodent-repellent granules.

In addition, Pastion Plus rodent-control bait, containing the active ingredient Brodifacoum, was distributed at a rate of two 12-gram pieces per tent. The bait was placed in safe and concealed locations, away from children, food items, and water sources.

Prior to the commencement of the control activities, families received a refresher briefing reinforcing the awareness and safety messages delivered during the first round of the intervention, rather than participating in new awareness sessions. The briefing covered the necessary preparations before spraying the tents and the site, safe practices during implementation, ventilation and cleaning procedures, and the conditions for safely re-entering tents after spraying. Families were also reminded of the risks associated with touching insecticides or rodent bait and were instructed to immediately report any exposure incident or concern to the site team.

The intervention was implemented in accordance with the principles of protection, do no harm, and human dignity, with particular attention given to the safety of children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other individuals at heightened risk. Families were instructed to keep children, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and individuals with specific health conditions away from spraying areas. They were also advised not to place insecticides or rodent bait near sleeping areas, food preparation spaces, or water-storage facilities.

The activity further emphasized the rights of women and children to access a safe and healthy environment. Safety information was communicated in a clear and appropriate manner, while ensuring privacy, non-discrimination, and opportunities for families to raise questions and submit feedback or complaints related to the intervention.

The intervention was implemented in coordination with the site management and other relevant stakeholders. It contributed to reducing the prevalence of rodents and insects and mitigating the associated health and environmental risks, thereby enhancing the safety of displaced families and improving health and living conditions within the displacement site.

Primary Activity: Two-Way Information Sharing, Feedback and Complaints
Summary:
Date: Sunday, 25/01/2026
Location: Al-Khair Camp – Deir Al-Balah
Implementing Agency: Ma’an Center – Protection Department / Community Partnership Projects
Activity Type: Coordination meeting and community outreach with the camp committee and a field assessment visit

2. Objective of the Activity

To strengthen community coordination in the area of protection, assess the needs of women and children within the camp, identify cases requiring immediate intervention or referral to available protection services, and assess the overall camp environment in terms of safety and access to services.

3. Participating Parties

Protection Department Team – Ma’an Center (Community Partnership Projects)

Al-Khair Camp Committee (Community Committee Members)

Ma’an Center Field Team working in the camp

4. Activity Summary

A coordination meeting was held at the Ma’an Center’s activities tent inside the camp, during which key protection issues affecting camp residents were discussed, with a particular focus on the situation of women and children. An initial assessment of cases requiring intervention or follow-up by protection teams was conducted, and safe communication mechanisms with the local community were agreed upon. This was followed by a field visit within the camp to assess the site conditions, identify potential safety risks, and evaluate the overall environment from a protection and access-to-services perspective.

5. Outputs

Identification of a number of cases requiring intervention or follow-up by protection teams.

Documentation of key challenges related to the safety of women and children within the camp.

Strengthened coordination with the camp committee as a community partner in case identification and reporting.

Proposal to establish protection points within the camp to provide a safe space for residents to express their concerns and challenges.

6. Challenges

Sensitivity of certain protection issues and difficulty in public disclosure.

Limited availability of safe and designated spaces to receive complaints or requests for support.

Need to strengthen community awareness of protection services and referral mechanisms.

7. Recommendations

Under the Community-Led Initiative (CLI) "Tent Free from Insects," the Site Management team will support a comprehensive vector and pest control campaign at Al Shaheed Jameel Site, Khan Younis, with the aim of improving public health and creating a safer living environment for displaced families. The initiative will focus on reducing the presence of disease-carrying insects and other harmful pests through site-wide cleaning activities, community awareness sessions, and the targeted application of approved pesticides and pest control treatments. Implementation will be carried out in close coordination between the Site Management engineering team and the CLI members, following a structured work plan that includes planning, procurement of pest control materials and personal protective equipment (PPE), scheduling of spraying activities, implementation, inspection, and quality assurance. Throughout the implementation period, the engineering team will provide continuous technical supervision to ensure that all pest control measures are conducted safely, effectively, and in accordance with health, safety, and engineering standards. Upon completion, the initiative is expected to significantly reduce pest infestations across the site, improve hygiene and environmental health conditions, and contribute to a safer and healthier living environment for all residents.

This ensures communities are well-informed and able to submit relevant and feasible proposals.

Summary:
SM implemented orientation session for the Community-Led Initiatives (CLI), under Site Management (SM) activities, aim to promote community participation, ownership, and self-reliance by supporting projects that benefit the wider community rather than individuals. These initiatives contribute to key objectives such as improving safety, social cohesion, environmental conditions, community services, and group-based livelihoods.
The number and budget of initiatives are defined at the project design stage, while their distribution is determined by the SM team based on needs and context, in coordination with other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication.
Site committees act as the main applicants, ensuring inclusive consultations with community members to identify priorities. Diverse and gender-balanced participation, particularly women’s involvement in leadership, is strongly encouraged.
To support transparent and effective implementation, the SM team conducts orientation sessions with site-Level Committees, explaining the CLI objectives, eligibility criteria, application process, and roles and responsibilities. This ensures communities are well-informed and able to submit relevant and feasible proposals.

The Site Management training session provided participants with an overview of site management principles and practices to ensure safe, dignified, and inclusive living conditions. It introduced the role of the Site Management Committee (SMC) in representing community members and supporting coordination with service providers.

The training covered key components including the Terms of Reference (ToR), Code of Conduct (CoC), and the roles and responsibilities of SMC members, emphasizing accountability, community participation, and effective communication.

It also highlighted the importance of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention and response, focusing on identifying risks, promoting safe practices, and ensuring appropriate referral mechanisms. It also introduces the CFM.

Overall, the training aimed to strengthen participants’ capacity to support effective, protection-focused site management.

A total of 31 participants (17 youth and 14 elderly) took part in the discussion, highlighting significant challenges faced by men and persons with disabilities. Before the crisis, individuals were engaged in various livelihoods, but currently, most struggle to meet basic needs. Persons with disabilities are particularly affected, with no access to employment and heavy reliance on family and community support. Access to food, services, and facilities is largely dependent on humanitarian aid and is often unequal, with major barriers related to infrastructure, distance, and lack of accessibility. Participants emphasized limited freedom in controlling resources and confirmed the absence of inclusive participation in community activities or decision-making processes, which are mainly led by site management. Key protection concerns include insecurity, lack of privacy, and inability to meet basic needs. The most urgent priorities identified were accessible services, financial assistance, and psychosocial support, alongside improving communication, representation, and safe spaces within the community.

A total of 19 participants (11 youth and 8 elderly) from Yafa site took part in the discussion, highlighting the severe challenges faced by men and persons with disabilities. Before the crisis, some individuals had access to formal and informal employment, while currently most men are unable to secure income and focus on meeting basic survival needs. Daily life has become highly constrained, with persons with disabilities heavily dependent on family members and community support. Access to food, non-food items, and services relies mainly on irregular humanitarian aid, with significant barriers such as long distances, poor infrastructure, and overcrowding. Participants confirmed inequality in access to resources and lack of control over them. There is no meaningful participation in community activities, and decision-making is centralized within site management, excluding persons with disabilities. Key risks include insecurity, poor living conditions, and lack of privacy. Priority needs include financial support, psychosocial services, improved infrastructure, and safer living conditions.

A total of 20 participants, including 15 adult women and 5 young women, took part in the discussion, reflecting on the significant changes in their lives after displacement. Participants described pre-war life as stable and organized, while current conditions are exhausting, with poor living environments, increased responsibilities, and emotional strain due to family separation and loss of livelihoods. Access to food depends largely on community kitchens and limited purchasing options, with some safety concerns reported. Views on access to and control over resources were mixed, and many participants expressed low trust in complaint mechanisms. Women, children, and persons with disabilities were identified as the most vulnerable groups, facing challenges such as lack of education, mobility issues, and heavy domestic burdens. Participation in activities is limited, and decision-making is controlled by service providers, often marginalizing women’s voices. Key needs include water, lighting, and basic shelter items, alongside improved safety measures and stronger communication channels.

At Al-Fedaa site, all 23 men, including 3 elderly, described a major shift from previously stable livelihoods to almost complete dependence on humanitarian aid. Men are mainly occupied with survival tasks such as securing food and water, facing high stress and limited income opportunities. Access to services is difficult due to overcrowding, long distances, and poor infrastructure, with persons with disabilities facing greater barriers. Living conditions are unsafe, with multiple environmental and protection risks. Participation in community roles is very limited, and decision-making remains centralized. Key needs include financial assistance, psychosocial support, improved infrastructure, safer conditions, and more inclusive engagement opportunities.

At Al-Shaheed Jameel site, all 12 participants, including 3 elderly, described a sharp decline from pre-crisis livelihoods to conditions focused entirely on survival. Persons with disabilities are fully excluded from employment and rely heavily on family and community support for daily needs. Access to services is extremely limited due to poor infrastructure and lack of accessibility, with significant inequality in resource distribution. Living conditions are inadequate, contributing to stress, social tensions, and insecurity. Participation in community roles is absent, and decision-making is centralized. Key needs include accessible facilities, financial assistance, psychosocial support, improved services, and stronger community engagement and communication mechanisms.

At Al-Jawhari site, all 13 participants, including 3 elderly, described a sharp decline from previously stable livelihoods to severe economic hardship and near-total dependence on humanitarian assistance. Men are largely unable to secure stable income and spend most of their time meeting basic survival needs, while persons with disabilities face heightened exclusion and dependency on others. Access to food, water, and essential services is inconsistent and constrained by long distances, overcrowding, and lack of accessible infrastructure. Living conditions are unsafe, with risks related to poor hygiene, disease spread, and inadequate facilities. Participation in community roles is absent, and decision-making remains centralized. Key priorities include financial support, accessible services, improved infrastructure, psychosocial support, and more inclusive engagement mechanisms.

Topic: Site Management Committee Establishment, Coordination or Planning
Summary: A coordination meeting was held at Al-Jawhari site with representatives of blocks and Acted SM team, aiming to organize fieldwork and enhance coordination. The meeting came in light of proactive field initiatives carried out by some committees, which required clarifying the governing organizational framework. Discussions focused on the importance of a clear organizational structure, defining roles, and improving communication mechanisms, in addition to adhering to the Memorandum of Understanding and the Code of Conduct. Emphasis was also placed on clear institutional representation and avoiding overlaps in responsibilities. It was agreed to form a committee composed of block representatives under the name “Monitoring Committee.”

At Al-Jawhari site, two women’s sessions (15 and 40 participants, including 1 and 3 elderly respectively) revealed a significant shift toward survival-based living and increased burdens on women. In the first session (15 participants), all reported no decision-making power, no active roles, and lack of safety, highlighting risks such as fear of exploitation, harassment, and ineffective complaint mechanisms. In the second session (40 participants), all confirmed increased responsibilities and reliance on community kitchens, while the majority reported unequal access to services and limited trust in feedback systems. Although participation was higher (40/40), awareness of representation structures remained low. Across both sessions, women identified children and elderly as highly vulnerable groups. Overall, findings reflect high vulnerability, limited control over resources, safety concerns, and the urgent need for improved protection, inclusive participation, better services, and empowerment opportunities.

At Al-Rimal Al-Thahabiea site, two women’s sessions (20 and 19 participants, including 2 and 5 elderly respectively) highlighted increased burdens and vulnerability among women. In the first session (20 participants), all reported significantly increased responsibilities, active participation (20/20), awareness of complaint mechanisms, and representation in site structures, yet all confirmed unequal access to resources and lack of safety due to environmental risks. In the second session (19 participants), all reported no active roles in decision-making, unequal access (19/19), and ineffective complaint systems, despite awareness of channels. Across both sessions, women and children were identified as the most vulnerable. Overall, findings show heavy workloads, limited control, safety concerns, and the need for livelihood opportunities, psychosocial support, improved protection, and stronger, more responsive community engagement mechanisms.

At Al-Fidaa site, two women’s sessions (16 and 15 participants, including 2 and 0 elderly respectively) highlighted significant challenges following displacement. In the first session (16 participants), all reported increased physical and environmental burdens, lack of awareness of complaint mechanisms (16/16), and unequal access to resources, despite relatively high participation (14/16). In the second session (15 participants), all confirmed increased stress, lack of privacy, and reliance on community kitchens, while most reported unequal access and mixed awareness of complaint channels. Participation was moderate (10/15), but decision-making remained externally controlled in both sessions. Across both groups, children, elderly, and persons with illnesses were identified as highly vulnerable. Overall, findings indicate high stress, limited control, weak feedback systems, and urgent needs for services, protection, and psychosocial support.

FGD  – Women > 50 Year
The discussion guide examines the roles and responsibilities of women within the community, comparing current conditions with the period before the crisis. It explores daily life, lived experiences, and levels of independence, including reliance on others for routine activities.
It also investigates access to food, non-food items, and essential services, focusing on how resources are obtained, controlled, and whether women have equitable access and decision-making power over their use. Special attention is given to physical accessibility of key facilities such as latrines, water points, health centers, and distribution sites, as well as challenges faced during service access.
The questions assess awareness of complaint and feedback mechanisms in cases of unequal access, and identify the most vulnerable groups in the community along with the underlying causes of their vulnerability.
Furthermore, the guide explores the priority needs of women, their participation in community activities, and the extent of their roles and influence in decision-making processes. It evaluates their representation within community leadership structures and gathers suggestions for improving their inclusion and advocacy.
Barriers preventing women from expressing their concerns are highlighted, alongside potential mechanisms to enhance their participation. The role of men and boys in supporting women’s involvement in decision-making is also examined.
Finally, the discussion addresses safety and protection concerns, including unsafe locations, risks faced by women, emergency preparedness, and access to support systems. It also gathers recommendations for creating a safer, more inclusive, and enabling environment for women in the community.

Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) were conducted across displacement sites to introduce the project and raise community awareness about the details of work within the sites, including planned activities, implementation mechanisms, and the role of the community in participation and follow-up. The sessions also aimed to collect feedback, identify needs and priorities, and strengthen transparency and communication.

The sessions included a presentation of project objectives and planned activities, followed by interactive discussions with participants to explore challenges and needs within the sites, as well as discussing the risks faced by residents such as safety concerns, lack of services, and environmental conditions. Dedicated sessions were also conducted with women and girls to ensure their perspectives are included in planning and decision-making.

Overall, the sessions demonstrated positive community engagement and a clear willingness to participate in the implementation of activities and improve living conditions within displacement sites.

Topic: Site Management Committee Establishment, Coordination or Planning
Summary: The meeting presented the ACTED SMC framework aimed at strengthening site management through a more structured, transparent, and efficient committee system. It reviewed the current SMC structure using a mapping exercise to identify gaps and improve alignment with site needs. Discussions focused on clarifying roles and responsibilities, enhancing coordination among committees, site representatives, and humanitarian actors, and improving decision-making processes. The Terms of Reference (ToR) was introduced as the main guiding document, alongside a proposed revised SMC structure based on sectoral committees (including data management, protection, education, health, WASH, security, and distribution) under a Site Representative and Deputy. Participants agreed on updating both infrastructure and service mapping to reflect current gaps and needs. Key principles such as inclusiveness, transparency, accountability, and clear roles were emphasized, along with agreed working mechanisms including regular meetings, structured decision-making, documentation, and performance monitoring. Capacity building for committee members was also highlighted as essential for effective implementation. Action points included updating mappings and progressing toward finalizing the SMC structure, with the next meeting focusing on reviewing updates and confirming final decisions.

Topic: Programming Specific Meetings (e.g. project inductions, cash for work, etc.)
Summary: The meeting introduced Community-Led Initiatives (CLI) as a new approach within displacement sites, highlighting ACTED Site Management’s supporting role. It provided an overview of Site Management duties and explained that CLIs are initiatives designed by communities to respond to their most urgent needs. Objectives include reducing life-threatening risks, improving environmental and social well-being, strengthening cohesion, and enhancing or establishing community services and livelihoods. The implementation process is community-led, with site committees coordinating idea collection and prioritization while involving wider residents. Each site will choose one initiative. ACTED will support through awareness sessions, guidance on applications, and continuous technical assistance.

Topic: Programming Specific Meetings (e.g. project inductions, cash for work, etc.)
Summary: This meeting aimed to introduce Community-Led Initiatives (CLI) and clarify ACTED Site Management’s involvement in their implementation. It presented the role of Site Management and defined CLIs as community-driven initiatives addressing priority needs in displacement sites. The objectives include reducing risks, improving environmental and social conditions, strengthening community cohesion, and supporting services and livelihoods. The approach ensures community participation through site committees and broader resident involvement in generating and prioritizing ideas. Each site will implement one selected initiative. ACTED will conduct awareness sessions, explain criteria and procedures, support application submission, and provide ongoing guidance throughout the implementation process.

The CCCM training was conducted for Site Management Committees (SMCs) to strengthen their capacity in effectively managing and coordinating within displacement sites. The session provided a clear overview of the roles and responsibilities of site committees, emphasizing their role in community representation, accountability, and facilitating communication between humanitarian actors and site residents. A key part of the training focused on the five core activities of CCCM, including coordination and partnership, information management, service monitoring, community participation, and site maintenance, with practical guidance on how to apply these activities to improve service delivery and living conditions. The training also covered the Code of Conduct, highlighting essential principles such as integrity, respect, non-discrimination, and professionalism in all interactions. In addition, special attention was given to PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse), ensuring that committee members understand their responsibilities in preventing, reporting, and responding to misconduct. Overall, the training aimed to enhance the knowledge and skills of site committees, enabling them to perform their roles effectively while promoting a safe, inclusive, and well-coordinated site environment.

The safety audit conducted at Tabaria alKhair site in Khan Younis identified serious protection, environmental, and infrastructure concerns affecting displaced families, particularly women and girls. The site hosts approximately 5,464 residents and experiences severe overcrowding . Tents are placed very close together, resulting in limited privacy and insufficient movement space for residents within the site.
The complete absence of night lighting creates major safety and protection risks, especially for women, children, and older persons. Poor visibility during nighttime movement has led to multiple accidents, including children falling into open pits.
Water access remains inadequate, with serious shortages affecting daily use. Although a water line exists within the site, supply is limited to once or twice per week, leading to tensions and disputes among displaced people during water distribution. Sanitation facilities are available but remain insufficient in terms of privacy and dignity, as multiple families are forced to share the same latrine facilities. In addition, there is no dedicated safe space for women, and the site management room is temporarily being used for women’s activities and awareness sessions.
The presence of open pits throughout the site poses severe safety hazards, particularly for children and older persons. A previous fatal incident involving a child falling into a pit was reported at the site. Waste accumulation is another major concern, contributing to foul odors, rodents, and deteriorating public health conditions, while residents continue to request improved waste removal mechanisms.
Seasonal flooding significantly affects the site due to differences in ground elevation and poor drainage. Rainwater accumulates in lower areas, flooding tents and damaging wooden structures within the site. The spread of stray dogs and insects, combined with the absence of proper site boundaries, has also contributed to increasing health risks, including skin diseases. The assessment highlights urgent needs for improved lighting, safer pathways, drainage interventions, sandbags, waste management systems, dedicated women’s spaces, safer sanitation facilities, and enhanced protection measures for vulnerable groups within the site.
12 out of 15 women in FGDs sessions reported no clear place to seek help or to refer protection cases in site.
